presentation.label: BREAK CUTTER
presentation.summary: Livecut's jungle break cutting on a sliced Flex track: repeats, stutters, warps, pushes and fills.
presentation.overview: BREAKCUT turns a sliced break on a Flex track into a cut-up, the way Livecut and Nick Collins' BBCut do: the break is cut into phrases of one to four bars, each phrase into blocks, each block into cuts that replay the block's start. CutProc11 repeats odd-length cuts and stutters at the end of a phrase; WarpCut plays blocks straight, as fast even rolls, or accelerating and ritardando; SQPusher pushes quavers and semiquavers by their place in the bar and ends a phrase with one of its thirteen fills. BREAKCUT writes the result as the track's trigs with STRT locks for the slices, RTRG and RTIM for cuts shorter than a step, micro-timing for cuts off the grid, PTCH for pitch ramps and RATE for reversed blocks. The stock sequencer plays it at the pattern's tempo, speed, length and swing.
highlights: Livecut's three cut procedures, and MIX to draw one per phrase
Rolls and stutters as retrigs, off-grid cuts as micro-timing
Pitch ramps on rolls, reversed blocks
Real trigs and locks: edit any step as usual; no clock of its own
usage: Load a break on a Flex track, slice it into a grid of one slice a step (16 slices for a one-bar break) and set SLIC ON in SRC SETUP.
Choose BREAKCUT in SRC SETUP's machine list. Set SLCS to the number of slices.

ALGO picks the procedure; ACTV sets how much it cuts, ROLL how often phrases end in a roll or fill; RAMP pitches the rolls, REV reverses blocks. Each turn rewrites the track; YES draws a new variation.

controls.name: ALGO
controls.doc: The cut procedure: Livecut's CutProc11, WarpCut and SQPusher, or MIX, one drawn per phrase

controls.name: SLCS
controls.doc: Slices in the break, one a step: 1-64 (stored as slices - 1)

controls.name: ACTV
controls.doc: How much it cuts: CutProc11's repeats (0-4), WarpCut's 1 - straight chance, SQPusher's activity

controls.name: ROLL
controls.doc: CutProc11's end-of-phrase stutter chance, WarpCut's accelerating share, SQPusher's fill chance

controls.name: RAMP
controls.doc: A roll's pitch at its end, -12..+12 semitones (12 none), as PTCH locks

controls.name: REV
controls.doc: The chance a block plays reversed (RATE locks)

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base loaded over USB (beta) with the machine table (ot_machines). Card firmware cannot include it.
Needs a Flex sample sliced one slice a step with SRC SETUP's SLIC on. The STRT value of a slice, RATE's reverse value and RTIM's scale are read from the unit and unverified here (TESTING.md).
BREAKCUT owns the PTCH, STRT, RATE, RTRG and RTIM locks, the trigs and the trig words of the steps inside the track's length; LEN, AMP, LFO and FX locks stay.
A step holds one trig: where a cut continues and another starts in the same step, the new cut wins. Accelerating rolls become even retrigs within each step.
Livecut's amplitude, pan, duty-cycle and effects are not ported. The seed is kept but not shown on a page; YES advances it and shows it.
Not yet run on hardware or in the emulator.

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: From the USB package build.py makes from the sources (m68k-elf-gcc 16.2, -Os): 7,696 bytes of ColdFire code and data and 1,784 of bss (the generator's state and a 64-step line), one instance, 139 relocations, no stock-code sites. No DSP memory, no heap.

processing.label: CPU load
processing.conditions: Work happens on the UI task once per knob turn or YES: one line of up to 64 steps and an in-place rewrite of the track record. Nothing runs while the pattern plays.

impact.conditions: A knob turn or YES on a BREAKCUT track; idle otherwise.

cpu.rationale: One line of at most 64 steps (at most 128 cuts a block) and an in-place record rewrite per edit on the UI task; nothing at interrupt level and nothing while playing.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code and no change to the DSP programs.

memory.rationale: 9,480 bytes of ColdFire code, data and state in DRAM (7,696 + 1,784 from the package header); the line it writes is the track's own record.

tests.summary: Host checks only: the cut procedures play the break straight when nothing cuts, produce well-formed, deterministic lines with stutters, fills, retrigs, micro-timing, pitch ramps and reverses; the RTIM scale, the track-record writer and the settings packing are checked under the sanitizers; the package's machine record sits at the registry's index (test_engine.py). Not run on a unit or in the emulator.

license.declaration: The cut procedures follow Livecut's BBCutter.cpp by Remy Muller (GPL-2.0-or-later, mdsp/Livecut 2695d386ebb23b13ceeb1a4aa76b6851ce9ea050), after Nick Collins' BBCut; SQPusher's fill table is carried over. The Octatrack glue is original, in the shape of VECTOR's MIT native.c. No Elektron firmware, extracted routines, tables, samples or dumps are included.

access.location: Flex track: SRC SETUP's machine list (double-tap SRC), BREAKCUT after the stock machines
steps: Load a break on a Flex track, slice it one slice a step and set SLIC ON in SRC SETUP. Double-tap SRC, scroll to BREAKCUT and press YES. The SRC page now holds ALGO, SLCS, ACTV, ROLL, RAMP and REV; SRC SETUP keeps the sample's own setup.
Push LEVEL on the SRC page for the stock sample controls and again to return; hold a trig for stock's page and its locks.
Double-tap the track key for the stock sample pool, as on any Flex track.
